text.p: Latvia's Olainfarm pharmaceutical company, which makes its debut on the local bourse on Monday, said it sees a 1997 production volume of 12 million lats, a rise of 7.67 million lats compared to last year.

"Distribution agreements in excess of $20 million have been signed with major Russian wholesalers, that will lead to a significant increase in sales in the last six months of 1997," Nikolay Stakanov, Olainfarm director, said in a joint statement with Hansa Investments.
Olainfarm earlier reported a first quarter loss of 1.62 million lats on turnover of 1.79 million lats.
The statement said that the 1997 first quarter interest and tax penalties item of 1.27 million lats "were one-off items that have little to do with the current operating performance of Olainfarm."

"The portion relating to penalties may be written off by the State Revenue Service if the company reschedules or cpitalises tax debts, which could lead to these written back to profit," Harry Rozenstein, associate director of Hansa Investment, said in the statement.
Olainfarm production in May was 1.12 million lats, a growth of 600,000 lats versus March, Stakanov said in the statement.
"The situation has stabilised," he said, referring to "the difficult situation inherited from the previous management".
"We intend (to have) an interim audit (carried out) by June 30 by an international accounting firm," Stakanov said.
